# How to use these prompt files

*Acme Retail · November 2026 · generated by ddreview 1.0.0 · facts.json c7ce712567c5*

Each file is self-contained: paste it into the LLM of your choice as it is. They hold aggregated tables only
(services, operations, calls, failure rates, p95). Identifiers inside resource names are masked; service, host and
dependency names, including internal host names and hosts named by IP address, appear as they do in the exports. No raw
spans and no timestamps below the minute are included. facts.json and the exports stay on your machine.

| File | Paste it to get | Then |
|---|---|---|
| `01-diagram-landscape.md` | a service map in Mermaid | replace the landscape Mermaid block under *What Datadog sees today*, then validate the notebook |
| `03-diagram-dependencies.md` | the failing-dependencies map | replace the dependency-map Mermaid block, then validate the notebook |
| `04-diagram-inside-payment-gateway.md` | the inside-a-request diagram for that service | replace the Mermaid block in that finding, then validate the notebook |
| `10-polish-findings.md` | the findings re-written in a smoother voice, every number kept | check the answer with `validate --text --against`, then replace the lead, table, bullets and actions of each finding; keep its diagram, live-graph and 🔎 lines |
| `11-exec-summary.md` | a 150-word leadership paragraph | check it with `validate --text --against`, then put it under the executive summary table |
| `22-month-over-month.md` | four sentences on what moved | check them with `validate --text --against`, then put them under *Since last month* |

The LLM may change wording, order of bullets and diagram layout. It may not change, round, drop or add a number, remove a
qualifier such as "without noise" or "in the 9-minute sample", or add a claim the tables do not support. `validate --against` compares the numbers of each section with the original notebook: a number added or changed is an error, a number dropped is a warning. `validate --text` alone only rejects a figure that facts.json cannot produce in any format, so a typo that happens to match another fact passes. Neither checks a value inside a Mermaid block: read the diagram against the tables before pasting it.
